subquestions.text_open: 8-5 Ethylene glycol is commonly condensed with carbonyl compounds to protect carbonyl groups. As shown below, '[R]C([H])=O' + 'SCCCS' → '[R]C1([H])SCCCS1'; '[R]C1([H])SCCCS1' + 'CCCCLi' → '[R]C1([Li])SCCCS1'. Thioacetals invert the polarity of the aldehydic carbon, and propane-1,3-dithiol is often used for this purpose. Briefly explain why ethane-1,2-dithiol, the sulfur analogue of ethylene glycol, is not used instead. (No more than 50 words.)

text_images.description: The figure shows a two-step reaction. The first step is '[R]C([H])=O' + 'SCCCS' → '[R]C1([H])SCCCS1', in which the carbonyl carbon has δ^+ character. The second step is '[R]C1([H])SCCCS1' + 'CCCCLi' → '[R]C1([Li])SCCCS1', in which the carbon bonded to lithium has δ^- character; R denotes an alkyl group.

rubric: The lithium salt obtained from ethane-1,2-dithiol readily undergoes fragmentation. (2 points; a correct reaction equation is also acceptable.)

subquestions.text_open: 8-6 Organic compound A (C_4H_6O_2) is oxidized by acidified potassium permanganate to give a single organic product B without gas evolution. B reacts with two equivalents of CH_3Li and, after workup, gives the major product C. C reacts with sodium metal in benzene and, after workup, gives D. Under sulfuric acid, D rearranges to E (C_6H_12O). Write the SMILES structures of A-E.
rubric: A is 'CC(=O)C(=O)C'; B is 'CC(=O)O'; C is 'CC(=O)C'; D is 'CC(C(C)(C)O)(O)C'; and E is 'CC(C)(C(C)=O)C'. (1 point each; 5 points total.)
